answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each account to post a bond before it can influence shared decisions. For example, a juniper agent may stake onyx tokens to join a river-market’s dispute process; if its rulings are later shown to violate a verifiable rule, the bond is slashed and honest participants are compensated. Creating many identities then requires many independently locked deposits, not just cheap accounts, while the threat of forfeiture makes Sybil attacks financially risky.
